sections.html:
Brownsburg is a town in Hendricks County, west of Indianapolis, with an estimated 34,089 residents in July 2025. The count was 28,973 in 2020, 21,285 in 2010 and 14,520 in 2000, roughly a doubling in twenty years. The town covers about 16.4 square miles, and White Lick Creek, a tributary of the White River, runs north to south just west of the center.

Three out of four homes are owner-occupied, so a typical Brownsburg sale is a single-family house, not a rental unit. The questions sellers ask are about condition, timing and equity.

sections.h2: Older houses in a fast-growing town
sections.html:
James B. Brown first settled the area in 1824, and the town was founded in 1835 as Harrisburgh. A post office opened in 1836 and took the name Brownsburg. Most of the housing is far newer than that history, which fits the growth since 2000.

A house that predates the recent growth may carry older systems, and a cash sale avoids spending money on updates that a buyer may want to redo anyway. Whether the house is new or old, the questions at sale time are the same: what condition is it in, what taxes are open, and what permits were pulled.

US 136 is the main east-west road and State Road 267 the main north-south road, and both connect to Interstate 74, which has two nearby interchanges. The town's economic development page also names Ronald Reagan Parkway as the industrial and distribution corridor linking I-74 to I-70 and Indianapolis International Airport.

Employers and draws listed there include:

  • Brunswick, a Fortune 500 company
  • Maplehurst Bakeries
  • LAPP USA, a German-based manufacturer
  • Lucas Oil Indianapolis Raceway Park, which hosts the NHRA U.S. Nationals
  • Three hospitals and a VA clinic

The average commute is about 24 minutes. Owners who relocate for work usually face tight timelines, and a closing date you set yourself can fit around a new job start.

sections.h2: Which school district covers a Brownsburg house?
sections.html:
Brownsburg Community School Corporation serves most of the town. A small part falls in the North West Hendricks Schools district, whose high school is Tri-West Hendricks High School. The Brownsburg district has eleven schools: eight elementary schools, two middle schools and one high school.

Families usually begin a house search with the district line, so confirm which district your address is in before you list it. A house in the smaller district may need a different explanation to a buyer. Private options include Bethesda Christian School and St. Malachy Catholic School.

Brownsburg uses an online permit portal, and the Development Services Department oversees planning and building. The Advisory Plan Commission reviews new development, and the Board of Zoning Appeals hears requests to vary standards such as setbacks. Town Hall is at 61 N. Green St., and the phone for these questions is (317) 858-6072.

Floodplain rules are in Chapter 152 of the town code. The Floodplain Administrator inspects work in progress, can issue a written stop-work notice and can revoke a permit tied to false statements. Records are public at Town Hall.

  • With unpermitted work, such as a finished basement or a deck, expect questions from buyers.
  • If your lot is near White Lick Creek, check its floodplain status before you assume a clean sale.
  • If you inherited a house, find out whether open permits exist before closing.

The town code, Chapter 152 has the enforcement language.

Hendricks County property tax comes due in two installments, May 10 and November 10 being the standard Indiana dates. A late payment inside 30 days costs 5 percent, and after that the penalty is 10 percent.

The Hendricks County Auditor's website has property values, sale history and tax details for each parcel. Pull your parcel record before you accept any offer so you know what the bill has been. Indiana tax bills arrive in spring, and the title company prorates the tax at closing.

The state due dates page and the town planning and building page have more detail.

Gather a short set of papers so a buyer and the title company can move quickly. Start with your latest Hendricks County tax bill and the parcel record from the Auditor's site. Add any permits you pulled for the house, plus a note of work done without one. If the lot is near White Lick Creek, include the floodplain status you found at Town Hall.

Then think about the mortgage. A payoff figure from your lender tells you whether the sale leaves anything after the loan and the closing costs. If it does not, say so early, because it changes which route makes sense. A cash sale at least shortens the time you keep paying a loan, taxes and insurance on a house you no longer want.

The town reports over 300 acres of parkland, four developed parks and 20 miles of trails, and three hospitals and a VA clinic serve the area. These details help a buyer picture daily life and are worth mentioning to anyone who asks about your house. They do not change the condition of the roof or furnace, which is what drives a cash offer.

sections.h2: What a cash sale looks like in Brownsburg
sections.html:
You tell us about the house, we review it, and if you accept the offer we close with a local title company on a date you choose. There is no lender, so there is no loan approval step that can fall through. Closing depends mostly on how fast the title company finishes its search and paperwork, and we can work around your move date.

Many Brownsburg sellers bought during the growth years and now want to move on without staging, showings or a listing agreement. Others inherit a house in Hendricks County and live far away, so a single closing by mail or remote signing is easier than managing a listing. Typical situations include:

  • Owners moving for work on short notice
  • Inherited homes with unknown repair needs
  • Houses with deferred maintenance after long ownership
  • Owners behind on payments who want to avoid foreclosure

We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to fix the roof, finish unpermitted work or update the kitchen before an offer. Ask for the offer in writing, confirm who pays each closing fee, and tell the title company about any open permit or tax balance so the closing statement is accurate.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Brownsburg, Indiana?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied housing units is $309,400 for 2020 to 2024. Your own number depends on size, condition and location, so treat the figure as a general reference only.

faqs.q: Which school district is Brownsburg in?
faqs.a: Most of the town is in Brownsburg Community School Corporation. A small part is in North West Hendricks Schools, which feeds Tri-West Hendricks High School. Check your address with the district.

faqs.q: When are Hendricks County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Indiana's standard dates are May 10 and November 10, moved to the next business day if they land on a weekend or holiday. Penalties are 5 percent within 30 days and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: Does Brownsburg have flood rules for homes?
faqs.a: Yes. Chapter 152 of the town code covers flood hazard areas and lets the Floodplain Administrator inspect work, issue stop-work notices and revoke permits. Records are available at Town Hall, 61 N. Green St.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Brownsburg house if it needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to fix the roof, finish unpermitted work or update the kitchen before an offer.
